subject: Re: Data residency & region-pinning questions (Acme Bank)

Subject: Data residency & region-pinning questions (follow-up)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the walkthrough of your use cases and the regulatory constraints for Acme Bank. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the open items on data handling and residency so your IT/security teams can review: 

1) PII & logging controls
- Can you confirm the types of PII you consider "sensitive" for model inputs? (full SSNs, account numbers, tokenized identifiers, etc.)
- For logs: do you require zero-log for inference requests, or is encrypted, retained-for-30-days allowable?

2) Data retention and deletion
- Your retention policy for transcripts and embeddings (e.g., 30 days, 1 year, indefinite) — any mandatory holds?

3) Region pinning & failover
- Primary requirement: all inference for US customers must be served from us-east-1 or us-west-2 only.
- Question: acceptable cross-region failover window if primary region is unavailable (automatic failover to eu-west-1 / ap-southeast-1)?
- Backups: do you require cross-region encrypted backups, or can backups be retained in-region only?

4) Technical evidence
- We can provide SOC 2 summary, encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, and a region-pinning design diagram. Which of these would help your procurement/security reviewers first?

Next steps I propose: 
- Marissa: can we prep a short packet (SOC2 summary + region-pinning diagram + short answers) for Alice/Bob by EOD Thursday?
- Alice: if you can confirm the PII list and retention window, we’ll tailor the packet to those controls.

Cheers,

Aditya Rao

Date: 2027-06-05T13:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency & region-pinning questions (follow-up)

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Sensitive PII: full SSN, full credit card PAN, unmasked account numbers, and any customer-provided KYC docs. Tokenized IDs that are non-reversible are OK.
- Logging: our baseline is "no persistent request logs with customer content" — we can accept ephemeral logs for 72 hours for debugging but they must be auto-deleted and never leave our control plane.
- Retention: transcripts for conversational support agents must be retained for 1 year for compliance; embeddings used for retrieval may be retained up to 180 days.
- Region pinning: primary service must be US-only. For failover, our security team prefers manual failover with documented runbook and approvals for cross-region (we cannot automatically fail to EU/APAC without a high-urgency exec approval).
- Backups: backups of model artifacts and any persisted content must be encrypted and stored in-region (US) by default; cross-region replication requires an exception process.

I'll loop Bob (on IT infra) to confirm whether they need the network diagram or a high-level design first. For procurement, SOC2 summary + explicit statement on log retention & deletion process should be sufficient.

Best,
Alice
Director, Digital Platforms — Acme Bank
alice.jenkins@acmebank.com

Quick internal recap and action items based on Alice’s response: 

Summary of requirements from Acme:
- Sensitive PII: SSN, PAN, unmasked account numbers, KYC docs (no retention unless explicitly approved)
- Logs: no persistent customer content logs; ephemeral debug logs up to 72h, auto-delete
- Retention: transcripts = 1 year; embeddings = 180 days (needs to be configurable per-project)
- Region pinning: US-only primary; cross-region failover requires manual approval & runbook
- Backups: in-region encrypted only by default; cross-region replication via exception

Action items:
- Marissa -> Draft a 2-page packet: (1) SOC2 summary + (2) region-pinning diagram + (3) explicit answers on log retention/deletion and retention windows. Target: 2027-06-06 EOD. (I’ll assemble the SOC2 summary and Laura can produce the diagram.)
- Laura -> Produce a simple topology diagram showing region pinning, failover flow (manual approval), and where backups live (in-region by default). Deliverable: PNG.
- Aditya -> Confirm we can support per-project configurable embedding retention (up to 180 days) and articulate technical mechanism for auto-deletion of ephemeral logs at 72h.

Notes for packet language: emphasize manual failover workflow and that cross-region backups are available but require exception and written approval. Also include notes on KMS/HSM support for customer-managed keys to satisfy encryption controls.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks for the fast clarifications — very helpful. Per Marissa’s note, we’ve attached the SOC2 summary and a region-pinning diagram that shows: in-region serving (us-east-1 / us-west-2) only; automated in-region backups by default; cross-region replication and failover are supported via documented exception process (manual approval required).

Short technical answers to your bullets: 
- Ephemeral logs: Redwood supports request-level logging that is retained in an encrypted, access-controlled store for up to 72 hours, after which a scheduled job securely deletes content (we can provide pseudocode/runbook for your infra team).
- Embedding retention: per-project configurable TTL; we can set default to 180 days and expose retention policy via the Console + API.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for both at-rest encryption and backup encryption.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm the PII list and retention windows align with your compliance needs.
2) If acceptable, let’s schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security/IT (Bob) next week to walk the runbook and diagram. I’m available Tue/Wed 10–2 PT.
